As an Assembly Operator in mechanical engineering, you work independently on complex high-tech machines. From robots to transport systems: technical and varied. Wie zoeken we? As an Assembly Operator, you are a technical professional who not only assembles but also understands what happens when building a machine. You can work independently from drawings, recognize deviations and think practically about solutions. Experience with larger machines or installations is important, as you will work with technically complex systems here. MBO diploma in mechatronics, mechanical engineering or electrical engineering. Experience with machine building, equipment assembly or industrial assembly. Experience with larger machines, installations or comparable equipment. You can independently read and apply technical drawings. Knowledge of mechanical and/or mechatronic modules. You speak Dutch or English. Wat bieden wij je? You'll have plenty of freedom to apply your technical expertise broadly as an Assembly Operator. One moment you're working on a larger machine construction, the next on a robot, conveyor, or mechatronic module. With multiple assembly departments, you can continue to vary your work and develop yourself technically. A salary of €3,319 to €3,923 gross per month on a full-time basis, depending on relevant experience. 27 vacation days. 13 ADV days. A temporary employment contract with prospects of a permanent position. One-time bonus payment. Technical training and courses tailored to your experience and development goals. Opportunity to develop your skills more broadly by gaining experience across different assembly departments and techniques. Functieomschrijving You'll join an international machinery manufacturer in Lichtenvoorde where high-quality machines for the food processing industry are developed and built. Within assembly, different teams work closely together. Craftsmanship and quality are central, but sharing knowledge and solving technical problemstogether are also part of how we work. As an Assembly Operator in machinery manufacturing, you'll have considerable independence in assembling, inspecting, adjusting and testing machines and modules. The work ranges from large constructions to smaller mechatronic modules. Depending on the project, you might work on robotic solutions, conveyors or service and overhaul work. This variety ensures that even experienced machinery manufacturers remain technically challenged. Independently assemble modules and complete machines. Mount mechanical and mechatronic components. Work on larger machine constructions, robots and transport systems. Read and apply technical drawings. Perform inspections, adjustments and functional tests. Ensure quality of your own work. Identify and resolve technical deviations. Collaborate with engineering and other production departments. Contribute ideas on feasibility and improvements in the assembly process. Do you have experience in machinery manufacturing and are you looking for more technical variety and responsibility? Apply as an Assembly Operator in machinery manufacturing. Here you'll have the space to apply your craftsmanship broadly and continue to develop it.

As an Assembly Worker, you build high-tech machines and learn various techniques. Varied work where you can grow significantly. Wie zoeken we? Engineering should be something you genuinely enjoy working with. You find it interesting to discover how individual components come together to form a complete machine, and you work carefully because quality matters in assembly work. You don't need to have seen everything already: technical insight, curiosity, and the ambition to work increasingly independently are just as important. An MBO qualification in mechatronics, mechanical engineering, electrical engineering, or a comparable technical field. Affinity with mechanical and/or mechatronic engineering. You can read and apply technical drawings. You speak Dutch and/or English. Wat bieden wij je? You'll have the opportunity to gain broad knowledge of mechanical engineering here. Working across different assembly departments means you won't spend years doing the same task-instead, you'll work with a variety of machines and techniques. As an Assembly Worker, you build mechanical and mechatronic components, modules and ultimately complete machines. It's precisely this variety that makes this job interesting. There are different assembly departments, which means you'll work with a range of techniques. Think of robot assembly, mechanical conveyors and service assembly. You work on smaller components and larger systems, and sometimes you might be doing something different from one project to the next, or even from one day to the next. Assembling mechanical and mechatronic components and modules. Working according to technical drawings and work instructions. Building modules into complete machines. Inspecting, adjusting and testing assembled components. Identifying and reporting technical deviations. Working safely with professional tools and available equipment. Collaborating with experienced technicians and other technical departments. Contributing ideas for improvements within assembly.
